<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Business and economy
*[[Google]] starts deleting consumer accounts from its social network [[Google+]] due to low user engagement and the discovery of [[security vulnerabilities]] which potentially exposed user data to developers. [https://www.theverge.com/2019/4/2/18290637/google-plus-shutdown-consumer-personal-account-delete (''The Verge'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**[[Boeing]] delays the availability of the software update for its [[Boeing 737 MAX|737 Max]] airliners. The [[Federal Aviation Administration]] anticipates the update to be rolled out "in the coming weeks." [https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/boeing-faa-more-time-needed-737-max-fixes-1.5080823 (CBC)]

;International relations
*[[Russia–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Russia]] opens a helicopter training facility in [[Venezuela]]. Under the plans, Russian state-owned [[Rostec]] will train Venezuelan pilots to operate [[List of Mil Mi-24 variants|Mi-35M]] gunships and transport helicopters. The move comes after the White House warned Moscow against sending troops or military equipment to the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-politics-russia/russia-says-it-has-opened-helicopter-training-center-in-venezuela-idUSKCN1RE1G3 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*According to a criminal complaint filed in a U.S. District Court, a [[Chinese people|Chinese]] woman is arrested and charged with making a false statement to the [[United States Secret Service]] after illegally entering [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Mar-a-Lago]] resort in [[Florida]] on 30 March 2019 while carrying multiple passports, four mobile phones and a [[thumb drive]] containing [[malware]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-47795513 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-intruder-idUSKCN1RE2HW (Reuters)]
*Eric Holder (not to be confused with [[Eric Holder|the former U.S. Attorney General]] of the same name) is arrested and charged with the murder of rapper [[Nipsey Hussle]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2019/04/02/police-name-nipsey-hussle-murder-suspect-after-stampede-breaks-out-memorial/?utm_term=.7865bd46c335 (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[Peru|Peruvian]] authorities investigate the death of British [[De La Salle Brothers|De La Salle Brother]] Paul McAuley, age 71. According to the report he is burned to death in a home he founded for indigenous students in [[Iquitos]], in the northeastern Amazonian region. [https://apnews.com/article/a93ff0b209cd4d3285c753fbcdb6a653 (AP)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Algerian protests]]
**[[President of Algeria|President]] [[Abdelaziz Bouteflika]] resigns amid pressure from the public and the military, having ruled the country since 1999. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-47795108 (BBC News)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]] gives a speech after seven hours of continuous meetings, saying that a further extension to the withdrawal from the European Union is needed, and asking for talks with [[Jeremy Corbyn]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-47794235 (BBC News)]
*The chairman for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] in [[North Carolina]], [[Robin Hayes]], is charged with bribery and other corruption charges, along with Republican donor [[Greg Lindberg]]. [https://ca.news.yahoo.com/north-carolina-gop-chair-major-162449942.html (Yahoo!)]
*[[SNC-Lavalin affair]]
**Canadian Prime Minister [[Justin Trudeau]] expels former ministers [[Jody Wilson-Raybould]] and [[Jane Philpott]] from the [[Liberal Party of Canada]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-47754193 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-canada-politics-expulsion/canadas-trudeau-expels-two-ex-ministers-from-ruling-party-in-bid-to-end-scandal-idUSKCN1RE2IY (Reuters)]
*[[2019 Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The [[Nicolás Maduro]]-aligned [[2017 Constituent National Assembly|Constituent National Assembly]] formally strips opposition leader and [[National Assembly (Venezuela)|National Assembly]] [[President of the National Assembly of Venezuela|President]] [[Juan Guaidó]] of his immunity from prosecution, potentially paving the way for his arrest. [https://www.brisbanetimes.com.au/world/south-america/venezuela-s-guaido-stripped-of-immunity-20190403-p51aap.html (''Brisbane Times'')]

;Sports
* In [[American football]], [[Thomas Dundon|Tom Dundon]], principal owner of the [[Alliance of American Football]], announces that the league has suspended operations effective immediately, before the end of [[2019 AAF season|its first season]]. [http://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/26423928/aaf-suspends-operations-polian-disappointed (ESPN)]
